bottom_line: Empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.90).
implications: These data support that, over a median of 26.2 months, empagliflozin was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure than placebo (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.90; P<0.001). The reported hazard ratio for cardiovascular death alone (0.91; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.09) does not establish a reduction in cardiovascular death in this document. Uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial in HF with EF >40%.
major_points.quote:
EMPEROR-Preserved was a randomized, double-
blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, event-
driven trial.

major_points.text: Patients with class II–IV heart failure and ejection fraction >40% were randomized to empagliflozin 10 mg daily or placebo on top of usual therapy.
major_points.quote:
we randomly assigned 5988 patients with class II–IV
heart failure and an ejection fraction of more than 40% to receive empagliflozin
(10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to usual therapy.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (time to first event).
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

major_points.text: Primary composite outcome occurred in 13.8% with empagliflozin vs 17.1% with placebo (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.69–0.90; P<0.001).
major_points.quote:
a primary outcome event occurred in 415 of 2997
patients (13.8%) in the empagliflozin group and in 511 of 2991 patients (17.1%) in
the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.90;
P<0.001).

major_points.text: Safety: serious adverse events were numerically lower with empagliflozin; uncomplicated genital/urinary tract infections and hypotension were more common with empagliflozin.
major_points.quote:
Serious adverse events occurred
in 1436 patients (47.9%) in the empagliflozin
group and in 1543 patients (51.6%) in the pla-
cebo group.

absolute_effects.text: Primary composite outcome: 415/2997 (13.8%) with empagliflozin vs 511/2991 (17.1%) with placebo; 6.9 vs 8.7 events per 100 patient-years.
Hospitalization for heart failure: 259 (8.6%) with empagliflozin vs 352 (11.8%) with placebo.
Number needed to treat to prevent one primary outcome event over a median trial period of 26 months: 31 (95% CI, 20 to 69).
absolute_effects.quote:
During a
        median trial period of 26 months, the number of
        patients treated with empagliflozin needed to
        prevent one primary outcome event was 31 (95%
        CI, 20 to 69).

absolute_effects.text: Total number of hospitalizations for heart failure: 407 with empagliflozin and 541 with placebo.

subgroups.text: Effect on primary outcome was generally consistent across prespecified subgroups, including diabetes status at baseline.
subgroups.quote:
The effect of empagliflozin on the incidence
of primary outcome events was generally con-
sistent across prespecified subgroups, including
patients with or without diabetes at baseline

harms.text: Serious adverse events occurred in 47.9% with empagliflozin vs 51.6% with placebo.
harms.quote:

harms.text: Adverse events leading to discontinuation of treatment occurred in 19.1% with empagliflozin vs 18.4% with placebo.
harms.quote:
Adverse events leading to discon-

harms.text: Uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were more common with empagliflozin.

inclusion_criteria.text: Men or women ≥18 years with NYHA class II–IV chronic heart failure and LVEF >40%.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
Participants were men or women, 18 years
of age or older, who had New York Heart Asso-
ciation functional class II–IV chronic heart fail-
ure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of
more than 40%.

inclusion_criteria.text: NT-proBNP >300 pg/ml, or if atrial fibrillation at baseline NT-proBNP >900 pg/ml.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
The protocol required patients
to have an N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic
peptide (NT-proBNP) level of more than 300 pg
per milliliter or, for patients with atrial fibrilla-
tion at baseline, an NT-proBNP level of more
than 900 pg per milliliter.

exclusion_criteria.text: Excluded if they had a disorder that could change their clinical course independent of heart failure, or any condition that might jeopardize safety or limit participation.
exclusion_criteria.quote:
Patients were excluded if they had a disorder
that could change their clinical course, indepen-
dent of heart failure, or if they had any condition
that might jeopardize patient safety or limit
their participation in the trial.
